formulas.purpose: Measure uncertainty in a normalized probability distribution.
assumptions: input values can be normalized into a probability distribution
failureModes: Entropy measures uncertainty only; it does not identify which option is correct.

workedExamples.name: fair binary distribution
workedExamples.interpretation: A fair two-way uncertainty has one bit of entropy.

formulas.notation: D_KL(P || Q) = sum_i p_i log_b(p_i / q_i)
formulas.purpose: Measure directional distribution shift from reference Q to observed P.
assumptions: P and Q describe the same ordered event space
invalidInputs: zero q_i where p_i is positive
failureModes: KL divergence is directional; swapping P and Q changes the result.

workedExamples.name: binary shift
workedExamples.interpretation: The observed distribution has measurable directional shift from the reference.

formulas.purpose: Measure mismatch between a target distribution and an encoded/predicted distribution.
assumptions: P and Q describe the same ordered event space
invalidInputs: zero q_i where p_i is positive
failureModes: Cross-entropy can rise because of mismatch, uncertainty, or both; inspect entropy and KL when interpreting.

workedExamples.name: binary mismatch
workedExamples.interpretation: The encoding is worse than the one-bit entropy baseline by the KL divergence amount.
